name: Next.js
title: Next.js analytics, cookieless and EU-hosted event tracking
description: Add product analytics to your Next.js app with the @openpanel/nextjs SDK. Cookieless by default, event data stored in Germany, and setup takes a few lines.
tagline: Cookieless analytics for Next.js, with event data stored in Germany.
intro: Privytics tracks page views and custom events in Next.js apps through the @openpanel/nextjs SDK. You add one component to your root layout, point it at the Privytics ingestion API, and client-side route changes start registering as screen views. Setup is a few lines, and nothing is written to the visitor's device.

why.title: App Router navigations are counted
why.body: A Next.js app server-renders once and then navigates on the client. With trackScreenViews enabled, the SDK listens for those soft navigations, so every route change registers instead of only the first page load.

why.title: One package for client and server
why.body: @openpanel/nextjs exports the OpenPanelComponent and useOpenPanel hook for the browser, plus the OpenPanel class for Route Handlers and Server Actions. Client and server events land in the same project.

why.title: Survives serverless function shutdown
why.body: On Vercel a function can return before an in-flight request resolves, which silently drops events. Wrapping the call in waitUntil keeps the function alive until the event is sent.

why.title: No consent state to thread through layouts
why.body: The default setup sets no cookies and stores nothing on the device, so there is no consent flag to pass down your layout tree or gate the component on. You remain the data controller and decide what your own lawful basis requires.

steps.title: Add the component to your root layout
steps.body: apiUrl points the SDK at Privytics instead of its default host, and is the one prop you must set. scriptUrl is optional: the component injects the tracker script tag for you and falls back to OpenPanel's CDN when you leave it out, so set it if you want the script served from Privytics too. This prop only exists on the Next.js component.

steps.title: Track a custom event in a client component
steps.body: useOpenPanel is a hook, so the component needs the 'use client' directive.

steps.title: Track events from the server
steps.body: Server-side calls authenticate with a client secret, so keep this instance out of client components. On Vercel, waitUntil stops the function from closing before the event is sent.

faq.q: Why is the package called @openpanel/nextjs and not @privytics/nextjs?
faq.a: Privytics runs on the open-source OpenPanel engine, and the SDKs are OpenPanel's packages published under the @openpanel npm scope. You install the real package and point apiUrl at https://api.privytics.com. Privytics is independent and is not affiliated with or endorsed by OpenPanel.

faq.q: Does it work with the Next.js App Router?
faq.a: Yes. You add OpenPanelComponent to app/layout.tsx and it tracks client-side route changes when trackScreenViews is set. The package also supports the pages directory.

faq.q: Do I need a cookie banner for this?
faq.a: The default setup writes no cookies and stores nothing on the visitor's device. The anonymous visitor id is a salted hash of IP, user agent and project id, and the salt rotates daily. You are still the data controller, so confirm what your own lawful basis and local rules require.

faq.q: How do I track events from Server Actions or Route Handlers?
faq.a: Import the OpenPanel class from @openpanel/nextjs and create an instance with your client id, client secret and apiUrl. Call op.track from any server context, and wrap it in waitUntil on serverless platforms so the function does not exit first.

faq.q: Can I link events to my own user ids?
faq.a: Yes, via identify with your own profileId, which gives cross-session user profiles. That is opt-in and goes beyond the cookieless default, so you need your own lawful basis for it.

omitted: The upstream docs' 'Server side' section shows `import { OpenpanelSdk }` and `opServer.event(...)`. Neither exists in the SDK source: the exported class is `OpenPanel` (re-exported from @openpanel/web via `export * from '@openpanel/web'`) and the method is `track()`. I used the verified names, which also match the docs' own 'Server components' snippet. The upstream page contains a stale example.

CONFIRMED: the `scriptUrl` value https://privytics.com/op1.js is served by the Privytics marketing site itself (the file lives at apps/public/public/op1.js). It is optional: the component defaults to OpenPanel's CDN and works without it. It is set here only so the tracker is served from a domain we control.

createRouteHandler (the ad-blocker proxy from @openpanel/nextjs/server) was left out. It accepts an apiUrl option, but its script-proxy target is a hardcoded constant pointing at openpanel.dev/op1.js with no override, so a fully Privytics-hosted proxy setup could not be shown accurately.

The `filter` option (a stringified function) and `globalProperties` are documented upstream and exist in the component's props, but were omitted to keep the setup path short. They were not verified against a Privytics deployment.

Session replay config was omitted from the snippets. `sessionReplay` is a real option on the web SDK type, but the Next.js doc page shows no Next.js-specific example, and replay is paid-plan and opt-in per project.

The earlier claim that client and server events 'share the same client id' was cut. Server calls use the same client id plus a client secret; nothing in the source ties client and server events to a shared visitor/device id, so the stronger identity claim was unverifiable.

The earlier claim that the Pages Router is set up 'using _app instead' was cut. The SDK does support the pages directory (there is an explicit pages-dir ESM fix in index.tsx), but no upstream doc specifies _app placement.
Salt rotation was described as 'rotates daily' rather than 'midnight UTC'. The cron pattern is `0 0 * * *`, which is midnight in the worker's configured timezone, not necessarily UTC.
Exact SDK version pinning was not included. npm reports latest as 1.5.1 (MIT), while the local checkout is a fork build labelled 1.5.1-local.
No Privytics-hosted docs page for this SDK was confirmed to exist, so docsUrl points at the upstream OpenPanel page.
